nvdiffrast.how: exported with git archive; csrc/, nvdiffrast/, setup.py and pyproject.toml equal upstream's tag v0.4.0 (253ac4fcea7de5f396371124af597e6cc957bfae), the fork's three commits after it add build outputs and a .gitignore only
nvdiffrast.license: NVIDIA Source Code License for nvdiffrast (non-commercial; LICENSE.txt in the wheel's dist-info)

why: the wheel it replaces (nvdiffrast-0.4.0-cp311-cp311-win_amd64.whl, sha256 153c8c63c88ef7aab6ec5f48597c4c44d799693a1e80d09b9aaed5df495f145d) had host code built with /arch:AVX2: BMI2 shlx/shrx/sarx/bzhi at 22 sites, some run at import, so on a CPU with AVX but no AVX2 (Sandy / Ivy Bridge, i7-4930K) Pixal3D's server died while starting. This build has no /arch (MSVC x64's SSE2 baseline); its GPU code is built for the same architectures
version: 0.4.0+spellcast3d.1: a new version, so that pip replaces an installed 0.4.0 (with the same version it answers 'already installed' and keeps the old binary); a constraint nvdiffrast==0.4.0 still accepts it
python: CPython 3.11 of code\venvs\pixal3d (tools\python), setup.py build_ext; the wheel is the shipped wheel's files with the rebuilt extension and the new version (RECORD rewritten)
msvc: Microsoft (R) C/C++ Optimizing Compiler for x64, toolset 14.44.35207 (vcvars64), /O2 /GL /MD, no /arch; CL and _CL_ unset
cuda: CUDA 12.8 (nvcc V12.8.93) at C:\Program Files\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\CUDA\v12.8
cpu_instructions: legacy SSE / VEX scalar code 198 / 0, BMI2 0, FMA 0, AVX2 12 (the C runtime's CPU-checked strlen / memchr); the replaced pyd: 0 / 221, BMI2 22
checks: rasterize (+db), interpolate (+da), texture linear and mipmapped, DepthPeeler 2 layers bit-equal to the replaced wheel on an RTX 3060; antialias within its own run-to-run noise (atomics: 431 of 1.57 M values by <= 1.2e-7 against the replaced wheel's 464 against itself); a 1536 tall_man through a fresh install decodes the same mesh; pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps and the RECORD check clean
build_command: code/logs/profiling/release-check-2026-11-19/windows/tools/build_nvdiffrast.bat (setup.py build_ext inside vcvars64, MAX_JOBS 16, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1), then the extension swapped into the shipped wheel
rebuild: Spellcast3D's code/release/wheels/nvdiffrast/build_nvdiffrast_win.bat (https://github.com/IgorAherne/spellcast3d): the same source, compiler settings and GPU architectures, as a wheel built from the source; `prepare_release.py scan-cpu <wheel>` there tells whether a build runs on a CPU without AVX2

runtime_requirements.install: pip install <this wheel>  (install.py installs every wheel in the whl folder)
